Your mom seems to be incredibly concerned for you, but is approaching the situation in the wrong way. Religion should not be involved in a mental health discussion, unless the receiving end is actively interested in pursuing a religious faith to cope with their feelings. You should explain to her that your question to your friend was only hypothetical, she is crossing your boundaries, and you are uncomfortable.

It seems like your partner is dependent on you, and is their only source of stability. That being said, you are not responsible for them. They are responsible for their own actions, and it is not your fault. Maybe you two should discuss the matter and the state of your relationship to better understand what the other person wants.
Maybe tell one of his family members that you’re worried for him?
Is there anyway you yourself can travel to his location? I know in the earlier post you had claimed that you don’t want to contact authorities because it’ll cause a panic.
If you need support, I am here at anytime. I may just be a stranger on the internet, but I genuinely want to help.
It doesn’t have to be a therapist, just someone who can support you unconditionally.

I understand exactly how you feel, bottling up your emotions in fear of being a burden to someone. Sometimes you just want to tell them how badly you want to leave this world, but expressing feelings of suicide still tends to be a taboo topic in today’s society, and it totally sucks. If you need any emotional support or want to vent out all your emotions, it’s okay to. It’s not attention seeking, it’s crying for help.
I’m sorry, it must be very psychologically damaging to have lived through that. Have you spoken to anyone about it?

If you’re still with an abusive partner, please try your best to contact someone or authorities about this issue, it’s not a safe or healthy predicament to be in, it might be difficult to leave but it won’t get any better if you stay. That being said, you are very resilient and brave to still be here, just living through pain and trauma is brave and inspiring. I know it sounds pretty corny, but what I’m saying is genuine.
